---
title: "check-function-graphs.yml"
---

Diff-scoped check that flags a definition of a function of one or two inputs
with no graph of that function.
The lab's rule (Ezra, 2026-11-10) is that
every definition for a function of one or two inputs
includes a graph of that function,
in 2D for one input and in 3D for two inputs.
This implements
[gha#1838](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/issues/1838);
the writing rule is in
[psw#575](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/psw/pull/575).
It warns by default,
because spotting a function definition from its source is a heuristic.

## What it flags

A definition div (`#def-`) is a candidate
when the left-hand side of its first display equation,
up to the first `=`, `:=`, `\eqdef`, `\coloneqq`, `\triangleq`, or `\equiv`,
is exactly a named function applied to one or two arguments:
`f(x)`, `f(x, y)`, `\sigma\paren{z}`, or an f-form macro such as `\logitf{p}`.
Each argument must be a lowercase Latin or Greek letter,
with an optional subscript or superscript.
An uppercase letter names a set, an event, or a random variable,
and a vector or matrix macro (`\vx`, `\mA`) or an expression is not a scalar input either,
so a definition with such an argument is not a candidate.

The check reads only the first display equation outside HTML comments,
so a definition that states its defining equation second is skipped.
Any `=` counts as defining,
so a first equation that states a property of a named function, such as `\log(x) = y`,
makes the div a candidate.

A candidate passes when its div holds a graph,
which is anything `check-exm-figures` counts as a figure:
an image, a `fig-` labelled chunk, a `fig-` labelled div, an `@fig-` reference,
or an include of a `_fig` subfile.
A figure after the div does not count;
the graph goes inside the definition, after the defining equation.

A div holding an HTML comment `<!-- no-graph: reason -->`
with a non-empty reason is exempt,
for a function with no meaningful graph, such as one defined on a finite set.
Use `paths-ignore` to exempt whole paths.

## Scope

Only a definition that holds a line a pull request adds is reported,
so untouched definitions are not reflagged.
An added line whose exact text was also deleted in the same diff
counts as moved rather than new, and a blank added line is not content.

With no `base-ref`, or when the diff cannot be computed,
the check skips instead of scanning the whole tree.
Set `whole-tree: true` to scan every tracked file on purpose,
which measures how many existing function definitions lack a graph.
Every run that does not skip prints how many lines, files,
and candidate definitions it examined.

## Inputs

| Input          | Type    | Default       | Description |
| -------------- | ------- | ------------- | ----------- |
| `globs`        | string  | `'*.qmd'`     | Space-separated git pathspecs of tracked files to check (recursive by default). |
| `paths-ignore` | string  | `''`          | Comma- or newline-separated glob patterns (relative paths) to skip. Supports `*`, `?` and recursive `**`. |
| `fail`         | boolean | `false`       | Fail the workflow on a finding. The default is warning annotations only. |
| `whole-tree`   | boolean | `false`       | Scan every tracked file in full instead of only a PR's added lines. |
| `python-version` | string | `'3.x'`      | Python version to set up. |
| `runs-on` | string | empty (`CI_RUNNER` variable, else `ubuntu-latest`) | Runner label for the job. Use a self-hosted label only for a private repository; never for a public one, whose pull requests can run arbitrary code on it ([#1167](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/issues/1167)). |

## Permissions

Only `contents: read` (the default), so no `permissions:` block is needed.

## Example

```yaml
# Copy to .github/workflows/check-function-graphs.yml in your repo.
name: Check function graphs

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  check:
    uses: Morrison-Lab/gha/.github/workflows/check-function-graphs.yml@v3
    # with:
    #   fail: true         # block on a finding (defaults to false)
```
